sources.locator: Executable finite distribution fixture; no external source verification claimed

intuitive.text: Squared error combines variation around the estimator's mean and displacement of that mean from the fixed target. A constant estimator has zero variance but can still have squared error.
assumptions: The target is fixed and the estimator has a finite second moment.
intuitive.bridge: Spread and displacement become variance and squared bias when the square is expanded and averaged.

intermediate.text: For target 2, an estimator equal to 1 or 3 with equal probability has mean 2, variance 1, bias 0 and MSE 1. Adding 1 gives mean 3, variance 1, bias 1 and MSE 2.
assumptions: The two estimator values each have probability one half.
The target 2 is a fixed scalar, not another random observation.
intermediate.bridge: This finite distribution example illustrates the expectation identity without replacing the general derivation.

formal.text: Write T-theta=(T-E[T])+(E[T]-theta). Expanding and taking expectation gives E[(T-theta)^2]=Var(T)+(E[T]-theta)^2 because E[T-E[T]]=0. A finite second moment makes all these terms finite.
assumptions: T is a real scalar estimator with finite second moment.
When T and theta have units u, MSE and variance have units u squared; bias has units u.
formal.bridge: The centered cross term vanishes by the definition of expectation. No assumption of unbiasedness or normality is required. Infinite second moments fall outside this finite identity.
